Subject: Encryption/KMS follow-up — FinSolutions discovery call

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so both sides are aligned:

Call summary:
- Primary use case: customer support automation ingesting transcripts and attachments (PII present in ~10% of records).
- Scale: initial pilot ~50k requests/month, production target ~1M requests/month in 6–9 months.
- SLA expectations: sub-200ms median gen latency for short queries; audit logs required for all requests.

Encryption & data handling follow-ups you asked about:
1) In-transit encryption:
   - All traffic to Redwood is TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3). We use mutual TLS for Dedicated/Private deployments when customers request it.
2) At-rest encryption:
   - All persistent storage (model caches, logs, artifacts) is encrypted at rest using AES-256.
3) Customer-managed keys (CMK / KMS):
   - Hosted: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (CMK) for workspace-level storage encryption. You can rotate keys on your schedule and control grants.
   - Dedicated/Private: We support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with integrations to AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. HSM-backed keys (Cloud HSM / Azure Dedicated HSM) are supported in Private deployments.
4) Logging & retention controls:
   - Request/response logs can be configured per-route. Default retention is 30 days for hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can set custom retention policies and opt-out of storing request payloads.

Attachments: I attached a short factsheet on encryption options, a one-page KMS options spreadsheet, and our latest SOC 2 snapshot.

Next steps / actions:
- You: confirm if you require BYOK for the pilot and whether HSM-backed keys are a must.
- Us: schedule a technical deep-dive with our SEs to cover KMS integration and logging controls (we suggested Tue next week).
- I’ll loop in our SRE/Infrastructure (cc’d) for any region/residency requirements.

If useful I can also put together a quick mutual action plan with milestones and handoffs.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) For the pilot we need BYOK (customer-managed keys) and prefer HSM-backed keys for key material. Is that supported out-of-the-box for hosted or will this require a Private deployment?
2) Audit logs: we need immutable request/response logs retained for 12 months for compliance. Can logs be exported to our S3/GCS bucket or SIEM (Splunk)?
3) Data residency: pilot data must remain in us-west-2. Can you guarantee region restriction for model inference and logs?
4) If we move to Dedicated, what does the operational model look like for key rotation — do you manage rotation or does our security team keep sole control?

Also can you confirm whether any customer-deployable artifacts (e.g., model artifacts, cached KV stores) ever contain plaintext PII? We need to be explicit on whether any transient decrypted material is ever written to disk.

If we can get written answers to the above before the SE call that would be great — security team will triage those answers.

Thanks,
Sam Wong
Head of Engineering | FinSolutions
sam.wong@finsolutions.com

Thanks Sam — answers inline below and next steps at the bottom.

1) BYOK/HSM support:
   - Hosted: hosted workspaces can use customer-managed keys via AWS KMS CMKs, but HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM) require a Dedicated or Private deployment because we need dedicated hardware boundary and network isolation for HSM key access. For your requirement (HSM for key material), we recommend Private deployment.
2) Audit logs/retention/export:
   - Logs are exportable. For hosted/Dedicated we provide push/export connectors to S3/GCS and SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog). For Private deployments you can fully control where logs land. Immutable retention (WORM) can be configured on the target storage (e.g., S3 Object Lock).
3) Data residency:
   - We support region pinning for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we can route to specific cloud regions but cannot provide hard guarantees unless using Dedicated/Private. For your pilot in us-west-2 we recommend Dedicated in that region or a Private VPC deployment for strict guarantees.
4) Key rotation/operations:
   - BYOK model: customer holds the key material and controls rotation through their KMS. Redwood requests grants as needed (rotating access grants). For Dedicated/Private, customers retain sole control over key rotation; Redwood can provide automated tooling to re-grant as keys rotate.
5) Plaintext PII at rest/transient:
   - Our design minimizes plaintext persistence: transient decrypted data may be present in memory for processing; we do not persist plaintext to disk in permanent storage. Model KV caches and intermediate artifacts are encrypted at rest; you can opt out of storing request payloads entirely. For Private deployments we can implement stricter in-memory only processing patterns if required.

Attachments included earlier (re-attaching SOC2 snapshot and KMS summary).

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule SE deep-dive (90 minutes) to walk through KMS integration, network diagrams for Private, and logging export. Suggested times: Tue 2026-06-16 (10–11:30 PT) or Wed 2026-06-17 (8–9:30 PT).
- I’ll open a short MOP (mutual action plan) in HubSpot and include milestones for pilot BYOK configuration and SOC2 evidence review.

Please confirm which time works and whether FinSolutions wants the Private deployment discussion included.

Best,
Marissa
